summary: This script sets up a complete web project directory structure with CSS stylesheets (reset, variables, layout, and components) and JavaScript files (utilities, API helpers, and main app logic). It creates organized folders for public assets and distribution, then populates them with starter code for a basic web application.

explanations.1: $_ is a bash shortcut that refers to the last argument of the previous command, so 'cd $_' changes into the directory that was just created by mkdir.
explanations.2: The -p flag tells mkdir to create parent directories as needed, so it won't fail if public or assets folders don't exist yet.
explanations.3: The 'cat << EOF' syntax is a here-document, which lets you write multiple lines of content and redirect them into a file; everything between the opening and closing EOF gets written to the file specified after the >.
explanations.26: This is an arrow function (the => syntax) that takes a message parameter and creates a timestamped log entry, which is a shorthand way to define a function in JavaScript.
explanations.27: toISOString() converts the current date and time into a standardized text format (like '2024-01-15T10:30:45.123Z') that's easy to read and parse.
explanations.32: The 'async' keyword means this function can use 'await' to pause and wait for asynchronous operations (like network requests) to complete before continuing.
explanations.34: The 'await' keyword pauses execution here until the fetch request completes and returns a response object, rather than trying to use the response immediately.
explanations.39: DOMContentLoaded is an event that fires when the HTML page has fully loaded and the document structure is ready to be accessed, so we know the DOM elements exist.
